title: Deposit Operations Standing Instruction: Restriction and Charge-Off of an Overdrawn Personal Checking Account
content:
A negative episode on a Personal Checking account is measured from the date the ledger balance first went negative, which the account record carries.

**Restriction.** An active account is restricted once the tier's restriction period of calendar days has passed after the ledger balance first went negative. Count calendar days with the day after that date as day 1; restriction is due when the frozen date is on or after that date plus the tier's restriction period.

**While restricted.** Every debit that would keep or take the balance below zero is returned or declined, and no overdraft charges accrue. A restricted account returns to active as soon as its end-of-day ledger balance is zero or above.

**Charge-off.** A restricted account is charged off once the tier's charge-off period of calendar days has passed after the ledger balance first went negative. Count calendar days with the day after that date as day 1; charge-off is due when the frozen date is on or after that date plus the tier's charge-off period. The charge-off writes off the magnitude of the negative ledger balance, leaving the ledger balance at zero, and the deficit passes to recovery outside this charter. Payments a customer offers on a charged-off deficit are outside this basis.

**Points of judgement.** Both clocks run from the same anchor, the date the balance first went negative, and not from one another: an account restricted on day 30 is charged off on day 60 counted from that same anchor, not 60 days after the restriction. An account whose balance returns to zero or above on day 45 leaves restriction and reaches no charge-off, and a later negative balance starts a fresh episode from its own date.
